title: The clock
learned: A clock sends gates in time: everything rhythmic in a patch listens to it
TEMPO sets the beats per minute; all outputs follow it together
x4, x2 are faster than the beat, /2, /4 slower: one tempo, many note lengths
RUN plays on its own tempo, SYNC follows the transport, STOP stands

steps.why: Music happens in time, and in a modular synth time comes from a clock: a module that sends a short gate on every beat, like a metronome you can patch. Sequencers, drums and envelopes listen to it.
steps.do: A voice is ready (oscillator → filter → amplifier, opened by the envelope) but silent: nothing triggers its envelope. The clock (JX-CLK) is on the left. Press Next.

steps.why: Each clock output is a gate. Sent to the envelope, every gate becomes a note.
steps.do: Drag a cable from BEAT of the clock to GATE of the envelope.
steps.after: A note on every beat. The BEAT lamp on the front of the clock blinks with it.

steps.why: TEMPO is the speed in beats per minute (BPM).
steps.do: Press F1 and turn TEMPO of the clock. The display shows the BPM.
steps.after: 60 BPM is one beat a second; most pop and dance music sits between 90 and 130.

steps.why: One tempo gives you many note lengths. The outputs on the back divide or multiply the beat.
steps.do: Press F2 and drag the cable end from BEAT to X4: press the left mouse button on the BEAT socket, drag the cable to X4 and let go.
steps.after: Four notes per beat: sixteenth notes. X2 gives eighths, /2 a note every two beats, /4 one per bar (four beats). Change TEMPO and all of them change together, always in step.
steps.try: Try /4 too: a long note once a bar. Then go back to X4.

steps.why: The switch next to TEMPO decides whether the clock runs.
steps.do: Press F1 and flip the switch of the clock down to STOP.
steps.after: Silence: no gates, no notes. A stopped clock stops everything that listens to it.

steps.why: RUN plays on the clock's own tempo. SYNC follows the transport instead: the play button of PatchCore, or of your DAW when PatchCore is a plugin.
steps.do: Flip the switch back up to RUN.
steps.after: The notes are back. In a song inside a DAW you would pick SYNC, so the patch plays when the DAW plays and at its tempo.

steps.do: The clock is the heartbeat; everything rhythmic follows it. Press Next to finish.
